text.title: Feel Good Remorse
text.declared_genre: Alternative Hip-Hop / Acoustic Folk / Spoken Word
text.declared_mood: Guilty, wry, defensive, cautiously hopeful → warm, grounded, quietly defiant
text.production_notes: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar with a percussive busker groove, Lo-fi hip-hop drums with soft kick, brushed snare, and hand taps, Warm upright-style bass, Sparse piano enters after second hook, Subtle room tone for intimacy, Live imperfect close mix, Full-stop dropouts before punchlines, Final third adds soft harmonies and warmer bass, staying raw and uncluttered
text.vocal_notes: Intimate male vocal, Spoken-word rap verses with conversational phrasing, dry comic timing, and careful pauses, Soft indie-folk sung hook with fragile warmth, Starts apologetic and self-mocking, becomes more open and gently defiant, Close-mic verses, slight rasp on punchlines, occasional whispered doubles on repeated phrases, Final section more melodic and relieved
section_names: Verse 3 – warmer spoken rap | piano enters

transcription.text: I have a confession, which is annoying because lately, I've been trying not to turn every good day into a courtroom, but here it is, I feel good, suspicious, I know. Ten years back, I was basically a weather warning with shoes, low pressure in the hallway, heavy chances of not replying, small craft advisory fair, anyone trying to love me before noon, I wore the end of the world like a wink coat, buttoned it wrong, slept in it, called it realism and now, now I wake up and make little things, a tiny app for a friend who forgets their groceries, a dumb little game where the frog is sad, but financially responsible, a song like this, which is cheaper than therapy, and less likely To ask about my childhood with the clipboard And somehow that makes people nervous Like joy is only valid If it arrives by hand, covered in mud With references I know the room is wide I can hear the sirens hum But I found a little doorway Where I used to find a wall Maybe it's not on fire Maybe it's not all flood, maybe I'm allowed to feel I have without the train anyone Maybe I can keep my eyes open and still let the morning come Maybe it's not all ruined, maybe some things help someone I said maybe please lower the pitch fork to a conversational angle Everybody keeps telling me, be careful, which is fair, I am careful. I check the label, I check the lock, I check the thing that checks the thing that worry. The checker has hobbies, I don't trust the lad, just because it reaches higher, I test the wrong, I shake the frame, I keep one hand on ordinary doubt, but there's a difference between caution and throwing away the window because sunlight has a story even rude. They say it'll make you lazy, which is funny Because I have learned more in two strange years And funny respectable ones, where I sat politely Beside my own confusion, they call it discipline now And I don't understand something I can ask badly Repeatedly at midnight, with examples with follow-up questions That would make a teacher Stir out the window and reconsider cheese farming And yes, sometimes the answer wears a fake mustache So check, but sometimes it opens a door I didn't know had hinges Maybe it's not all fine or maybe it's not all flooded Maybe I'm allowed to feel lighter without betraying anyone Maybe I can keep my eyes open and still let the morning come Maybe it's not all ruined, maybe some things helps someone And yes, I hear the warnings, I hear the power bills, the server farms The men in expensive jackets are promising the future with very hydrated faces I hear the teachers die of the art, are scared, the workers asking if the latter is being pulled up While everyone claps with the elevator, I hear it I'm not asking you to stop worrying, I'm asking If there is room inside the world for one old and every person who was rounding quietly and found a tool that helped them breathe long enough to make something kind for somebody else is that allowed or do I need to be miserable again for the argument to stay tidy because I remember when everything felt finished not dramatic finished just dishes in the sink Finishing red message, finisher standing in a shop pile Holding two kinds of rice and feeling unqualified To continue as a person finished And now I make things small, things no empire, no prophecy No blowing portal, just a friend says Could it remind me and I say maybe Just the melody catches on the bat I'd have to know and I'll follow in Until the beam stops biting Just a question used to shame me It turns into a staircase, and I know stairs can lead anywhere The basement's included, so I bring a torch, I'm bringing that I bring the back of plans in the suspicious little face But I'm still going, not because everything is safe Because not everything that helps you has to be holy Not everything dangerous is useless Not every new door is a trap Just because the old runs were honest about hurting Maybe it's not all fire Maybe it's not all flood Maybe I'm allowed to feel fire Without betraying anyone Maybe I can keep my eyes open And still let them warn me to come Maybe it's not all ruined Maybe some things help someone Maybe it's not all feelings Maybe I'm not wrong For building little bridges Out of questions and sounds Maybe I can stay careful But still not come and done Maybe it's not all ruined Maybe some things help someone. So yes, I feel good. I'm a checking exits. I'm reading a small print. I'm keeping my doubts well-fed and hydrated, but for once, when the world says, be afraid. I can say, I am. And also, look what I made.
